purpose: Elevation sources approved for grading the bicycle routing graph, beside the Copernicus sources of map-platform/config/topography-source-policy-v2.json. Each terrain source is used inside its own area, and the first listed gives a post that two could. Offline maps and the map-platform image do not read this file.

terrain.title: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second seamless DEM
terrain.coverage: Conterminous United States: the posts inside the area, from the cells that touch it
terrain.areaSource: OpenStreetMap relation 148838 version 1054 of 2026-11-11, the boundary of the United States with its territorial sea, cut to longitudes -126 to -65 and latitudes 23 to 51. (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
terrain.attribution: Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program.
terrain.modifications: Cut to the area, resampled from 1/3 to 1 arc-second posts, rounded to whole metres, and joined to Copernicus GLO-30 opened by a grey-scale morphological opening, whose posts are lifted to meet 3DEP over 16 posts at the edge of 3DEP's data. Not endorsed by the USGS.

terrain.title: Natural Resources Canada, Medium Resolution Digital Elevation Model (MRDEM-30), CanElevation Series, digital terrain model
terrain.coverage: Canada: the posts inside the area, from the cells that touch it
terrain.areaSource: OpenStreetMap relation 1428125 version 649 of 2026-11-01, the boundary of Canada with its territorial sea. (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
terrain.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Produced in part using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.
terrain.modifications: Pixels below -10 m or above 7,000 m, which cannot be ground, are dropped with the pixels within four of them. Cut to the area, resampled from the 30 m Lambert grid to 1 arc-second posts, rounded to whole metres, heights left in CGVD2013, joined to USGS 3DEP at the border as it is, and joined to Copernicus GLO-30 opened by a grey-scale morphological opening, whose posts are lifted to meet the terrain over 16 posts at the edge of its data. Not endorsed by Natural Resources Canada.
